plan: With a private value of $14, my goal is to maximize potential profit. In a sealed bid followed by an ascending clock auction, I want to set an exit price that balances winning probability with potential profit. Since values are independent and randomly drawn, I'll bid strategically near my true value. A bid around $13-$14 seems optimal - high enough to potentially win, but not so high that I risk negative profits if I win at a price close to my value.

In a single-round sealed bid auction with an ascending clock, the optimal strategy is to bid strategically based on my private value of $14. I want to maximize potential profit by considering how other bidders might behave. Since values are drawn independently and randomly, I'll aim to bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer. A bid around $12-$13 gives me room to potentially win while protecting some profit margin.

With a private value of $6, my goal is to maximize potential profit. In a sealed bid auction with ascending clock, I want to bid strategically. Since values are drawn independently, I'll aim to bid just above my value to maximize chances of winning while minimizing overpayment. A bid around $7-$8 seems optimal - high enough to potentially win, but not so high that I risk significant loss if winning price exceeds my value.
